company: Acrow Formwork and Construction Services Limited
title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Restricted Persons
tiers.description: All employees of the Group in possession of inside information; Key Personnel; staff who work closely with Key Personnel, in finance/accounts or strategic planning; other employees notified by the Board or Company Secretary; immediate family members of Key Personnel; and companies, trusts and entities over which Key Personnel or their immediate family have control.

tiers.name: Key Personnel
tiers.description: Directors, Company Secretary, chief executive officer of a portfolio company of the Group, all direct reports of the chief executive officers, and any other senior executive with authority and responsibility for planning, directing and controlling Group activities; distinguished for clearance (approved by the Chair) and, for the Chair personally, approved by another Director.

tiers.name: Chair
tiers.description: The Chair of the Board; distinguished only for clearance routing (clearance for the Chair, or family/entities connected to the Chair, is given by another Director, and the Chair notifies the Board of an intention to trade).

tiers.name: employees (excluding Restricted Persons)
tiers.description: Employees not on the restricted persons register; a lighter clearance process applies (notify Company Secretary or CFO, confirm no inside information) with no 3-month acquisition confirmation required.

definitions.hedging_definition: transactions or arrangements which operate to limit the economic risk of their security holding (including holdings of securities which are unvested or subject to a holding lock or other escrow) in the Company

windows.end_anchor: 24 hours following release of the Company's half year end results (Appendix 4D)
24 hours following the release of the Company's preliminary full year results (Appendix 4E)

windows.start_anchor: release of price sensitive information to the market
after release of half year or full year results, once the Board confirms in a minuted meeting that it holds no inside information

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Company may impose additional ad hoc Blackout Periods when considering sensitive information it may be obliged to disclose. Confidential: each employee and officer must keep the imposition of the additional restriction confidential and not disclose it to anyone inside or outside the Company, except as required by law.

rules.detail: Derivative products including exchange-traded and OTC options, warrants and rights over the Company's securities are expressly brought within scope of the policy, so are subject to the same prior notification/clearance procedure (s12) and Blackout Period bans (s10) as ordinary trades.
rules.evidence: This policy covers trading not only in the Company's securities ... but also in other rights and derivative products such as any renounceable or unrenounceable right to subscribe for a share or debenture or any warrant, exchange traded or over-the-counter option and any contract for difference issued in relation to the Company's securities.

rules.detail: Absolute ban, applying to all employees, officers and directors, on transactions that limit the economic risk of unvested entitlements under any equity-based remuneration scheme; no clearance route is offered for this specific prohibition.
rules.evidence: Directors, officers and employees are prohibited from entering into transactions or arrangements which limit the economic risk of participating in unvested entitlements under any equity based remuneration schemes.

rules.detail: A separate, broader clause permits de-risking arrangements over a person's security holding, expressly including holdings that are unvested or subject to a holding lock or escrow, subject to prior written clearance from the Approving Officer.
rules.evidence: Directors, officers and employees must not enter into transactions or arrangements which operate to limit the economic risk of their security holding (including holdings of securities which are unvested or subject to a holding lock or other escrow) in the Company without first seeking and obtaining prior written clearance from the appropriate Approving Officer.

rules.detail: The same general de-risking clause applies to a person's security holding at large, so fully vested and unrestricted shares may be hedged with prior written clearance.
rules.evidence: Directors, officers and employees must not enter into transactions or arrangements which operate to limit the economic risk of their security holding ... in the Company without first seeking and obtaining prior written clearance from the appropriate Approving Officer.

rules.detail: Monetisation (e.g. a prepaid forward sale) is not named, but section 15's list of 'other rights and derivative products' over the Company's securities is illustrative rather than closed, so a structure of that kind is likely caught and would need clearance under s12 and comply with Blackout Periods under s10.
rules.evidence: This policy covers trading not only in the Company's securities ... but also in other rights and derivative products such as any renounceable or unrenounceable right to subscribe for a share or debenture or any warrant, exchange traded or over-the-counter option and any contract for difference issued in relation to the Company's securities.

rules.detail: Outright ban on short selling, alongside a ban on short-term or speculative dealing.
rules.evidence: At no time may Restricted Persons engage in short term speculative dealing in the Company's securities or short selling the Company's securities.

rules.detail: Securities lending is not named anywhere in the policy.

Contracts for difference over the Company's securities are expressly listed as covered instruments, so are subject to the same clearance and Blackout Period regime; a short CFD position would also engage the short-selling ban.
rules.evidence: any warrant, exchange traded or over-the-counter option and any contract for difference issued in relation to the Company's securities.

rules.detail: Standalone, tier-unqualified statement that margin lending is prohibited outright, with no clearance carve-out stated here. This sits uneasily with s10.5, which treats agreements giving a lender rights over securities as clearance-approvable for all personnel, and with s16.1(f), which excludes a forced sale under an 'approved' margin lending arrangement from the policy altogether.
rules.evidence: This policy also prohibits margin lending and other secured financing arrangements.

rules.detail: Granting a lender rights over an interest in securities (a charge, lien or pledge) requires prior written clearance from the Approving Officer; applies to all directors, officers and employees.
rules.evidence: Directors, officers and employees must not enter into agreements that provide lenders with rights over their Interests in securities in the Company without first seeking and obtaining prior written clearance from the appropriate Approving Officer.

rules.detail: The general lender-rights clause in s10.5 (applying to all personnel) treats any secured financing as clearance-approvable, while s15 separately states margin lending and other secured financing arrangements are prohibited outright with no stated tier or clearance route. The two provisions are in tension.
rules.evidence: Directors, officers and employees must not enter into agreements that provide lenders with rights over their Interests in securities in the Company without first seeking and obtaining prior written clearance from the appropriate Approving Officer.

rules.detail: A holding of less than 3 months is treated as short-term/speculative and will normally not be approved; the rule may be waived in exceptional circumstances (e.g. to pay tax on vesting) via the same prior written clearance form. Restricted Persons are separately barred from trading within 3 months of any acquisition (other than DRP or option/rights conversion).
rules.evidence: Where a Security is held for a period shorter than 3 months, in the absence of other circumstances the Company is likely to consider that the trade of the Security short term or speculative. No sale or acquisition of shares will normally be approved within 3 months of an acquisition or sale. This 3 month rule may be waived in exceptional circumstances such as to pay tax related to performance rights.

clearance.evidence: in the case of the Chair, or family members of or entities connected to the Chair, another Director... Any clearance to trade can be given or refused by an Approving Officer in its discretion without giving any reasons. A clearance to trade can be withdrawn by an Approving Officer if new information arises or there is a change in circumstances.
in the case of any other Key Personnel, or family members of or entities connected to those Key Personnel, the Chair.

clearance.approver: Chief Financial Officer, after confirming with the Board (or, for exceptional-circumstances/Blackout Period requests, the Chair or in their absence a Director)
clearance.evidence: have been advised by the Chief Financial Officer in writing, (after having confirmed this with the Board), that there is no known reason to preclude them from trading in the Company's securities as notified, or the trade is to occur during an Open Trading Window.

clearance.approver: Company Secretary or Chief Financial Officer
clearance.evidence: notify the Company Secretary or Chief Financial Officer in writing of their intention to trade ... have been advised in writing by the Company Secretary or Chief Financial Officer that there is no known reason to preclude them from trading.

carve_outs: shares acquired from a dividend reinvestment plan
shares acquired via conversion of options/rights
waivable in exceptional circumstances, such as to pay tax related to performance rights
short_term.evidence: Where a Security is held for a period shorter than 3 months, in the absence of other circumstances the Company is likely to consider that the trade of the Security short term or speculative. No sale or acquisition of shares will normally be approved within 3 months of an acquisition or sale.

exceptions.evidence: if the person granting the prior written clearance is satisfied that the person seeking the clearance does not possess unpublished price sensitive information about the Company and the person seeking clearance is in severe financial hardship.

if the person granting the prior written clearance is satisfied that the person seeking the clearance does not possess unpublished price sensitive information about the Company and there are other circumstances deemed to be exceptional by the person granting the prior written clearance.
where trading is required for compliance with a court order or court enforceable undertakings or for some other legal or regulatory requirement.
transfers of securities already held into a superannuation fund or other saving scheme in which the director, officer or employee is a beneficiary.

an investment in, or trading in units of, a fund or other scheme (other than a scheme only investing in the Company's securities) where the assets of the fund or other scheme are invested at the discretion of a third party.
undertakings to accept, or the acceptance of, a takeover offer.

trading under an offer or invitation made to all or most of the security holders such as, a rights issue, a security purchase plan, a dividend or distribution reinvestment plan and an equal access buy-back, where the plan that determines the timing and structure of the offer has been approved by the Board.

a disposal of securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement where the arrangement had been approved by the Company in accordance with this Policy.
an acquisition of a security under an employee incentive scheme.

the exercise of an option or right under an employee incentive scheme, or the conversion of a convertible security, although exempt from the fullness of this policy still requires the individual wishing to exercise these options or convert these securities to request permission in writing or via email from the Chief Financial Officer.

trading under a non-discretionary trading plan for which prior written clearance has been provided ... where: (a) the director, officer or employee did not enter into the plan or amend the plan during a Blackout Period; and (b) the trading plan does not permit the director, officer or employee to exercise any influence or discretion over how, when, or whether to trade.

exemption_authority: Approving Officers (another Director for the Chair; the Chair for other Key Personnel; the Chair or a Director for other employees, per s10.4) may grant clearance to trade during a Blackout Period in exceptional circumstances (hardship, other exceptional circumstances, or legal/court requirement), and may waive the 3-month short-term dealing rule (s14). Decisions are final, binding and may be given or refused without reasons; a refusal must be kept confidential by the person who sought it.

bespoke_clauses.clause: This policy also prohibits margin lending and other secured financing arrangements. [cf.] Directors, officers and employees must not enter into agreements that provide lenders with rights over their Interests in securities in the Company without first seeking and obtaining prior written clearance ... [cf.] a disposal of securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement where the arrangement had been approved by the Company in accordance with this Policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The policy is internally inconsistent on whether a loan secured on the collared shares is banned outright (s15) or approvable with clearance (s10.5, s16.1(f)); a bank should seek the Board's own interpretation and written clearance before treating the collar's loan leg as permissible.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors, officers and employees must not put in place a non-discretionary trading plan in respect of their securities in the Company without first seeking and obtaining prior written clearance from the appropriate Approving Officer.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: If the collar or its unwind is structured as, or resembles, a non-discretionary trading plan, it needs prior clearance and cannot be entered into or amended during a Blackout Period, constraining timing and roll flexibility.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Where ad hoc Blackout Periods are imposed by the Company, each employee and officer of the Company must keep the imposition of this additional restriction confidential.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: An undisclosed extra blackout can block execution, unwind or settlement of the collar at short notice without the bank being told why.

bespoke_clauses.clause: such approval is valid for a period of 5 Business Days from the date of grant of approval or the time when I become aware of Inside Information which has not been released to the market (whichever is the earlier).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A cleared OTC collar trade must be priced and executed within 5 business days, or fresh clearance must be sought, adding execution timing risk.

bespoke_clauses.clause: companies, trusts and entities over which Key Personnel or their immediate family members have control ... immediate family members of Key Personnel (including spouses, de facto spouses and children).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Routing the collar or its financing through a family trust or controlled entity does not escape the policy; the same clearance and blackout restrictions apply.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A reconciliation of restricted persons trades against the appropriate approvals and record in the register will be completed each month. Any discrepancies will be highlighted to the board and followed up.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Settlement or physical delivery under the collar will be reconciled monthly against clearances on file, so any mismatch (e.g. an unapproved secured loan) is likely to surface to the Board.

summary: A funded collar is difficult to support cleanly under this policy. The derivative legs (purchased put and written call) are expressly within scope as 'derivative products' and OTC options, so they are Dealings requiring prior written clearance from the relevant Approving Officer (another Director for the Chair, the Chair for other Key Personnel, or the CFO/Board for other Restricted Persons), executed within 5 business days and outside Blackout Periods, and hedging of unvested plan securities is banned outright. The loan leg is the key obstacle: section 15 states baldly that 'margin lending and other secured financing arrangements' are prohibited, yet section 10.5 treats agreements giving a lender rights over securities as clearance-approvable for all personnel, and section 16.1(f) excludes a forced sale under an 'approved' margin lending arrangement from the policy altogether — an internal inconsistency that the Board would need to resolve or waive before a secured loan could proceed. If the Board takes the position that a cleared, secured facility is permitted, the collar and loan must still avoid the half-year/full-year and price-sensitive-information Blackout Periods, keep any Restricted Person's holding above the informal 3-month minimum hold, and be re-cleared for any amendment, roll or unwind. Given the express, unqualified prohibition in section 15, a funded collar should not proceed without first obtaining the Board's written confirmation that the secured loan is not caught by that provision.
